incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (Articles 26-55 governing Limited Liability Companies), as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 2310 of 2017); Commercial Registry Law; Food Safety Law No. 1 of 2017
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — One-Stop Shop, in coordination with the Commercial Registry Department of the Ministry of Trade and Industry
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Association (Aqd al-Ta'sis / Incorporation Contract) executed before a Notary Public and filed with GAFI
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Egyptian LLC; nominal capital is freely determined by the founders and declared in the Articles of Association. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid in cash or in kind at formation, with bank certification of the deposited proceeds required for GAFI registration; an escrow account is not statutorily mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the incorporation contract of the LLC is ratified and the share capital subscribed by the founding shareholders is accepted; (2) that the registered office be fixed at [registered address], Cairo, Arab Republic of Egypt; (3) that [Name] be appointed Managing Director and [Name] Company Secretary for a four-year term; (4) that management be authorized to open corporate bank accounts, execute tax registrations, and engage a certified public auditor; (5) that all filings with GAFI, the Commercial Registry, the tax authority and social insurance fund be approved; and (6) that the Managing Director be empowered to obtain export, food-safety and municipal licenses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (branches: Cairo, Alexandria, Suez Canal Economic Zone)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three ranked proposed names in Arabic and English via the GAFI online portal or physical one-stop shop. The name must not conflict with existing commercial registrations, trademarks, or names contrary to public order. Obtain the name reservation certificate valid for 60 days.
required_dossiers: Passport/National ID copies of all founding shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a revised name list within 10 days; re-submission is free of charge, and a formal appeal may be lodged with the GAFI Legal Department.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office (Office of Notary General, Ministry of Justice)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding shareholders or their duly attested attorneys (with Arabic power of attorney) must appear before the Notary Public with the approved name certificate and execute the Articles of Association. The notary authenticates signatures and issues the certified incorporation deed.
required_dossiers: Passport/National ID of shareholders and authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries missing signatures or defective attestations, cure the deficiency by appearing on the next working day with correct documents; re-execution before the same notary is permitted without a new application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Incorporation and Commercial Registry Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop / Commercial Registry Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Articles of Association with the GAFI One-Stop Shop with prescribed registration forms. GAFI concurrently registers the company with the Commercial Registry, allocates the Commercial Registration number, and issues the incorporation certificate.
required_dossiers: Declaration of registered office (title deed or lease)
GAFI application forms and fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a deficiency notification, respond within 15 days with corrected documentation. If registration is refused, appeal to the GAFI Deputy Chairman for Investment Affairs within 30 days; judicial review is available before the Administrative Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Tax Card Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — Central Directorate of Taxpayer Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Commercial Registration certificate and notarized Articles to the ETA to obtain the Tax Card and Tax Identification Number (TIN). Complete VAT registration via the ETA portal. This step is mandatory for customs clearance and export operations.
required_dossiers: Copy of Managing Director National ID/Passport
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ETA requests additional evidence, present the missing lease or identification files within 10 days. A formal complaint may be filed with the ETA taxpayer service committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Insurance and Labor Office Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI) and Ministry of Manpower Labor Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the LLC with NOSI as an employer and submit Form 1 listing all founding employees. Simultaneously, notify the local Labor Office of the workforce roster. This obligation arises from Social Insurance Law No. 148 of 2019.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of errors in the insurance file, submit a correction memorandum to NOSI; late-registration fines may be mitigated by voluntary disclosure before any NOSI inspection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Warehouse License and Food Safety / Export Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Municipality (Hayy) and Egyptian Food Safety Authority (NFSA) / General Organization for Export and Import Control (GOEIC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the municipal commercial warehouse operating license for the logistics/storage facility, including Civil Defense fire safety approval. Register the facility with NFSA as a food storage and handling operator and enroll with GOEIC for export records. Secure any required product conformity or halal certificates for destination markets.
required_dossiers: Lease or title deed for warehouse
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality or NFSA flags fire-safety or hygiene deficiencies, remediate within 30 days and request re-inspection; appeal against denial may be lodged with the licensing committee and subsequently before the Administrative Court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) for facility-class licensing, in coordination with the Local District Municipality (Hayy) for the commercial warehouse operating permit
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Commercial Warehouse Operating License with Egyptian Food Safety Authority Facility Registration (Exporter of Pre-Packaged Foodstuffs)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) — pursuant to Environmental Law No. 4 of 1994 as amended by Law No. 9 of 2009
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C (Environmental Screening Form only) — medium-scale food storage and distribution facility not requiring a Full EIA Report, subject to EEAA screening and registration clearance
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must comply with Law No. 48 of 1982 (BOD ≤ 60 mg/l, COD ≤ 100 mg/l, TSS ≤ 50 mg/l); solid waste handling per the Municipal Solid Waste Regulation of 2006; refrigerants and VOC emissions within Law 4/1994 permissible limits; stormwater must be channeled to the public network without illegal connection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Civil Defense Authority (mandatory before warehouse occupation, covering fire-load classification, extinguisher placement, exit routes, and thermal detection for tallow-based goods); structural load inspection report from a licensed engineer for storage racks; occupational health and safety clearance from the Ministry of Manpower, including workplace hazard assessment, ventilation, and food hygiene protocols.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA / المصلحة المصرية للضرائب), Ministry of Finance; unified portal: www.eta.gov.eg (tax card, CIT, VAT, e-invoicing/e-receipts platforms). Customs-side counterpart: Egyptian Customs Authority (ECA) operating the NAFEZA single window / ACI (Advanced Cargo Information) system; corporate incorporation: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the LLC before GAFI or the local Commercial Registry; obtain the Commercial Registration Certificate and company file number. Step 2: Obtain an Import/Export Card (exporters register with the Ministry of Trade and Industry / GOEIC) before undertaking export distribution of the hotpot soup base product. Step 3: File corporate tax registration with ETA within one month of commercial registration; ETA issues the Tax Card (بطاقة ضريبية) reflecting the unified tax ID and certifying the LLC as subject to CIT, VAT and stamp duties. Step 4: Register for VAT with ETA (portal or competent tax office) once taxable annual turnover exceeds EGP 500,000, or voluntarily at incorporation, and obtain a distinct VAT registration number. Step 5: Complete mandatory e-invoicing onboarding: procure the ETA client X.509 certificate, connect the ERP to the ETA REST API (v1.3+) or use the ETA web portal, and link export transactions to NAFEZA/ACI customs declarations. Step 6: Open a bank account with a CBE-licensed bank and align remittance instructions with Central Bank of Egypt rules so export proceeds can be evidenced and repatriated within statutory deadlines.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — an Egyptian LLC is a per se corporate tax resident under Law No. 91 of 2005, subject to CIT at 22.5% on worldwide income; no pass-through, flow-through or check-the-box recognition. Distributions to non-resident shareholders are generally subject to a 10% dividend withholding tax, treaty-reduced where applicable. SCZone/Investment Zones may offer special incentive regimes under Law 72 of 2017 and Suez Canal Economic Zone protocols, but the default statutory classification remains entity-level taxation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not operate a check-the-box regime; LLC tax classification is statutory. Available elections relevant to the export LLC: (i) consolidated corporate income tax filing for a fiscal group under Article 51 of Law 91/2005 where the parent holds at least 90% of capital and voting rights and both entities adopt the same fiscal year; (ii) immediate claiming of input VAT credits attributable to export zero-rated supplies (refund election under Article 30 of Law 67 of 2016) instead of carrying credits forward; (iii) tax loss carryforward election under Article 34 of Law 91/2005 for a maximum of five years, with no general carryback; (iv) advance pricing agreements and mutual agreement procedures under Egypt's treaty network for transfer-pricing and hybrid mismatch resolution. No hybrid mismatch 'reverse hybrid' election is recognized in Egyptian domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended; a unitary, credit-invoice VAT administered by the Egyptian Tax Authority with no provincial or sub-national indirect tax overlay.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory VAT registration threshold: EGP 500,000 annual turnover of taxable supplies under Law 67/2016 (Article 16). Exporters may register voluntarily before reaching that threshold in order to claim input VAT refunds; non-resident digital-service suppliers are subject to deemed registration with no threshold, and Egyptian business buyers self-assess on reverse charge for qualifying imported services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing with real-time fiscal clearance: every export supply invoice must be submitted to ETA in the official ETA XML/JSON schema, digitally signed with the ETA-issued X.509 client certificate, and transmitted through the REST API (v1.3+), a licensed middleware product, or the ETA portal; ETA validates and returns an acceptance UUID and QR hash within seconds. Without clearance, the invoice is legally deemed unissued, export refunds are suspended, and penalties accrue. E-receipts (B2C transactions) and NAFEZA Advance Cargo Information (ACI) registration are mandatory in phases, with all VAT-registered taxpayers covered through the January 2025 rollout; physical export additionally requires the ACI export message, a customs statistical declaration and the ETA frozen transaction codes for refund processing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods, including pre-packaged spicy tallow hotpot base bricks, are zero-rated (0% VAT) under Law 67 of 2016 where the goods are physically exported and delivered to a non-resident buyer within the statutory export windows (generally 30–90 days from supply, subject to customs extensions). Offshore services are zero-rated only when rendered to a non-resident recipient, effectively consumed outside Egypt, and supported by a written contract and foreign-currency payment; no domestic Egyptian use may occur. Input VAT directly attributable to the zero-rated export stream is refundable under Article 30 of Law 67 of 2016 through the electronic refund workflow and is subject to a documentary audit against customs and banking data.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: ETA-cleared e-invoice (XML, acceptance UUID and QR code) for the export supply
Certified commercial invoice and export sales contract (Arabic or bilingual)
Customs Export Declaration as released on the NAFEZA/ACI single window, showing the statistical value and applicable HS classification (2103.x/2106.x)
Bill of Lading (sea), Air Waybill (air) or CMR (road) naming the exporting LLC as shipper and the foreign customer as consignee
Packing list, certificate of origin (if claimed) and weight/delivery list
Inward remittance certificate or Swift MT103 evidencing foreign-currency payment credited to the LLC's Egyptian bank account
Central Bank of Egypt foreign-currency export declaration confirming timely repatriation of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA cross-matches e-invoice clearance data with NAFEZA customs releases, CBE remittance records and bank MT103 evidence. Any discrepancy triggers suspension of the refund, reversal of input VAT credited and re-issuance of the export invoice at 14% VAT. For fraudulent zero-rating, Articles 71–72 of Law 67 of 2016 impose repayment of the evaded VAT, a fine of EGP 20,000 to EGP 5,000,000, imprisonment of between six months and five years, and interest at 14% per annum from the original due date. Under Law 91 of 2005 (Article 133), willfully false export documentation in CIT refund claims carries a penalty up to 300% of the evaded tax and criminal liability; the exporter is also disqualified from the refund program and e-invoicing clearance for up to three years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) under the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020; the General Department for Foreign Exchange Operations and the Financial Stability/Anti-Money Laundering Unit jointly administer exchange-control enforcement, authorised-dealer licensing, FX position limits and cross-border reporting for all Egyptian resident entities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a market-driven managed float regime (post-March-2024 FX reform) in which the EGP is fully convertible at interbank market rates for current account purposes; import/export payments, services and profit remittances are free of quantitative ceilings when supported by the required documentary file (commercial contract, customs declarations, tax clearance). Capital account transactions remain registration-based: foreign direct investment inflows must be recorded with GAFI (Law 72/2017) so that the future repatriation of capital and 100% disposal of after-tax net profits can be executed without CBE approval; in practice, CBE FX liquidity pressure periodically creates a settlement queue for non-essential repatriations, so the EG-LLC treasury must maintain a 30-to-45 day USD liquidity buffer and pre-position dividends in a USD account when the interbank spread is attractive.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE export-currency rules, 100% of the invoice value of non-oil export proceeds must be repatriated through the Egyptian banking system within 90 days of customs release, extendable to 180 days for deferred-payment export contracts upon written approval. The former mandatory 75% surrender ratio (Decree 380/2004) was abolished in 2016, and under the current flexible regime there is zero mandatory EGP conversion ratio: the exporter may credit proceeds to a USD/EUR/CNY foreign-currency account with an authorised dealer bank or convert at the interbank rate at its chosen timing. Nevertheless, the CBE requires submission of the customs export release certificate (via CargoX/ACI platform), the shipment export declaration and a bank receipt-of-value certificate; any non-repatriated or late-repatriated proceeds are reported by the bank to the CBE, triggering administrative penalties under Law 194/2020 and potential suspension of the exporter's customs identification number.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow / GAFI Investment Account + USD/EGP Operational Account
USD/EGP Operational Account + Pre-export Finance and LC Facility
Multi-currency Trade Settlement Account (EGP/USD/EUR) + Export Proceeds Collection Sub-account
Operational Current Account + Trade Finance Overdraft
Corporate Operational USD/EGP Account + Post-shipment Discounting Line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium for ancillary outlays only. Egypt's Law 221/2020 on Fintech allows CBE-licensed non-bank financial companies to operate digital payment wallets, but no offshore fintech EMI (Wise, Payoneer, Revolut Business, or similar) holds a CBE banking licence enabling resident corporate deposit-taking, LC issuance or export-proceeds collection. Offshore EMIs may be used for small service payments (software, marketing, remote contractors) and for receiving sponsor/partner micro-funding, but they cannot serve as the primary cross-border treasury rail or fulfil Egyptian Customs/import-form requirements; all substantive FX and liquidity flows must clear through CBE-licensed dealer banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for a foreign-owned EG-LLC with FX and trade-finance needs. At least one authorised director or the Egyptian-resident general manager holding a full notarised Power of Attorney must appear in person at the bank branch for biometric identity verification, signature specimen registration and the CBE-mandated face-to-face customer due diligence interview under AML/CFT Decree 164/2021. Remote-only account opening is not offered for corporates requiring Letters of Credit or USD clearing; in exceptional cases, a bank may close the account with the GM attending and require a subsequent video-call verification of the non-resident shareholder, but the underlying policy remains that a natural person with signatory authority must be physically verifiable in Egypt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Abnormally high cross-border payment velocity with invoices routed through third-country pass-through accounts (China-Hong Kong-GCC) in the hotpot base/tallow trade.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO register tracing all shareholders above 10% to natural persons; notarised source-of-wealth declaration; full transaction conduit map; Hong Kong company registry extracts; three years of parent bank statements; and a written treasury policy that no third-party payment routing will be used without documented commercial rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared shipment value of tallow/hotpot base and customs or commodity benchmark price, flagged as potential trade-based money laundering or customs undervaluation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Loading inspection certificate issued by SGS, Intertek or CCIC for each consignment; proforma and final commercial invoices with Incoterms 2020; supplier factory cost card; third-party commodity exchange price quote; packing list; customs CargoX/ACI filing summary and a Cost-Insurance-Freight reconciliation sheet.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of open account/60-days deferred payment in the initial six months after account opening creating a discrepancy between goods flow and FX flow.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original signed supply contract with payment tenor; delivery and handover certificates from both sides; the Egyptian bank's in-country letter of guarantee or advance-payment bond; shipping documents (Bill of Lading, mate's receipt); customs release certificates; and a rolling 12-month receivable ageing schedule submitted to compliance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Food-grade and religious-certification risk for pre-packaged spicy tallow soup base exported to GCC/Levant importers (Halal chain integrity and shelf-life claims).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid Halal certificate from a recognised GCC certification body; ISO 22000/HACCP production evidence from the manufacturer; food-packing material safety declarations; batch-level lab reports; shelf-life stability data; export health certificate apostilled by Egyptian authorities; and the importer's registration documents showing legitimate distribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incoming capital injection from a sister-company in a low-tax or sanctioned-adjacent jurisdiction that may be characterised as a suspicious funding source.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: GAFI foreign-investment registration certificate for the EG-LLC; board resolution approving the capital increase; audited opening balance sheet; bank reference and transaction history of the remitting entity; legal opinion from Egyptian counsel confirming the inflow classification as equity versus shareholder lending; and a CBE source-of-funds questionnaire signed by the ultimate beneficial owner.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections should be executed via SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) from the foreign parent to the EG-LLC's USD account at the chosen Egyptian authorised-dealer bank, using the CBE Balance-of-Payments purpose code for direct investment equity and including the GAFI investment certificate reference in the narrative field for auto-classification. The funds are credited without prior CBE approval only when the GAFI registration material (board capital-increase resolution, amended shareholding structure and Ministry of Investment form) is pre-filed with the receiving bank; the bank subsequently issues an inward credit verification letter that serves as the legal basis for future dividend repatriation. For amounts above USD 250,000, supporting evidence of the parent's foreign corporate tax residence and a certified copy of the parent's constitution must be deposited; shareholders' loans must be expressly subordinated and declared on the bank's external-debt form to prevent reclassification as equity and to protect the future annual-interest remittance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements run on two primary rails: (a) SWIFT MT103/MT202 via the Egyptian bank's correspondent network (CHIPS/Fedwire in New York for USD) for open-account TTs, service fees and advance settlements, each instruction matched with the CBE importer declaration and the approved FX budget; and (b) Irrevocable commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700/MT707) issued under UCP600 for tallow and bulk-material purchases, with exporter presentations advised via MT754 and sight reimbursement executed against compliant documents; local EGP disbursements (customs duty, port charges, freight and payroll taxes) are cleared on the CBE Real-Time Gross Settlement system. To mitigate shipment delays, the EG-LLC treasury should request post-shipment discounting of LC export receivables at the AD bank and must maintain a 48-hour document-fixing window so that a single discrepancy notice does not trigger an overnight FX gap.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward outright USD/EGP contracts with Egyptian authorised dealing banks (tenor 1-12 months) for trade-related receipts and payments.
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/EGP executed by the non-resident parent treasury to hedge the translated Egyptian exposure without physical EGP settlement.
FX swaps (spot-next, tom-next, weekly, monthly tenor) with local banks for short-term USD/EGP liquidity levelling.
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EGP, EUR/EGP) with local dealing banks for long-term procurement and refinancing hedges.
Islamic treasury alternatives structured as parallel Tawarruq or wa'ad-based FX arrangements with the Islamic windows of CBE-licensed banks.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 21) with audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after fiscal year-end (by 30 April for a 31 December year-end); electronic filing extension available to 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fine of EGP 500-5,000; interest of 2% per month on unpaid tax; criminal prosecution and potential administrative suspension of commercial operations for repeated non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Withholding Tax and Salary Tax Reconcilement Return (Form 41)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March following the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly penalty of 2% on unpaid withheld amounts and late-filing fines up to EGP 5,000; withholding certificate denial can bar the company from export transactions and banking operations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory filing of audited financial statements and partners'/AGM minutes with the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office - GAFI / Ministry of Trade
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: General meeting of partners/AGM within 6 months of fiscal year-end; minutes and audited accounts filed within 30 days after the meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of EGP 2,000-10,000 under Companies Law No. 159/1981; escalating to administrative strike-off and deregistration of the LLC

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registration Renewal (5-year cycle) with Beneficial Ownership annual confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due every 5 years on the registration anniversary; UBO confirmation submitted together with the renewal application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension of commercial registration; loss of export legal capacity; bank account blockage; fines under Commerce Law No. 34/1976 and AML Law No. 80/2002; administrative strike-off after continued non-renewal

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Importer/Exporter Card Annual Renewal (Foreign Trade Registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Organization for Export and Import Control (GOEIC), Ministry of Trade
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before expiration of the card (valid for one year from date of issue)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Blockage of customs clearance and export of pre-packaged goods; undeclared export transactions treated as illegal foreign trade subject to forfeiture and administrative penalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Food Business Establishment License Renewal (pre-packaged food export warehouse and distribution)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual renewal filed not less than 30 days before expiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Immediate suspension of the food trading license; seizure of non-compliant pre-packaged hotpot soup base stock; criminal liability under Food Safety Law No. 1/2017

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit required for every LLC under Companies Law No. 159/1981 where paid-up capital reaches or exceeds EGP 250,000 (approx. USD 5,000) or where annual taxable gross sales exceed EGP 20 million (approx. USD 400,000); audit also compulsory for all taxpayers claiming exemptions or transfer-pricing adjustments and for any LLC whose revenues exceed double the ETA audit-turnover threshold. The export wholesale activity in this profile triggers statutory audit in all practical years due to licensing, letters of credit, and food export controls.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) issued by Decree No. 110/2015, fully converged with IFRS; entities with revenues below EGP 20 million may apply the simplified EAS aligned with IFRS for SMEs.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under AML Law No. 80/2002 and Executive Regulations (Cabinet Decision No. 1129/2019, as amended), every LLC must submit an annual beneficial-ownership declaration to the Commercial Registry in the same window as the Commercial Registration renewal or at the registration anniversary date, whichever comes first, confirming all natural persons exercising ownership or control (shareholding ≥10% or deemed control). Any transfer of LLC quotas, indirect shareholding change, or change in control must be reported within 15 days of the transaction, accompanied by the partners' resolution, updated quota ledger, and revised UBO disclosure; annual confirmation is refused if the register of members/quotas is not reconciled with the UBO statement.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors/Managers and their Powers
Minute Book of Partners'/General Assembly Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - 1,500 per year for a reliable corporate service provider in Cairo or the Suez Canal Economic Zone handling registry, tax, and food-law filings
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 7,500 per year for a licensed certified auditor (CPA-Egypt / member of the Egyptian Society of Accountants and Auditors) performing statutory audit and review of export sales, intercompany transactions, and financial statements

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 grants a 5-year tax holiday for new eligible projects in specified sectors or geographic zones, including free-zone companies subject to real economic substance; qualifying small and micro enterprises may be taxed under a flat-rate revenue regime of 0.5%–3% in lieu of the 22.5% statutory rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 15 (Corporate Income Tax Return), filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) online e-filing portal (in.gov.eg)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 4 months after the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year companies, no later than 30 April of the following year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name, trade registry number, tax card number, and registered address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an Egyptian permanent establishment (PE), enter the PE registration number and the foreign parent company details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the PE accounting period; it must align with the head-office fiscal year unless prior ETA approval has been obtained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales and revenue from commercial or industrial activity, including export turnover
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all Egyptian-source revenue attributable to the PE; revenue from offshore sales must be excluded unless effectively connected to the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold, operating expenses, and other deductible items
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductible expenses must be supported by valid invoices and contracts; cross-border related-party charges require a transfer pricing file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book profit or loss before tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute on an accrual basis in Egyptian pounds; attach reconciled financial statements for the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments: non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt income, and carry-forward losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back disallowed expenses and foreign taxes unless a DTA credit is claimed; deduct only the permitted loss carry-forward computed to year five.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income for the fiscal year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Same computation as for resident companies; no special rate for a non-resident PE.
Apply the 22.5% rate to the taxable income; do not offset foreign taxes at this line unless covered by a DTA credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance tax payments, withheld tax credits, and foreign tax credits under DTA
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the original residence certificate (TRC) and a credit schedule; the credit is capped at the Egyptian tax on the same income.
Pay the outstanding tax by the deadline via the ETA payment gateway; include the bank transfer reference.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: penalty of 5% of the tax due for the first month, plus 2% for each subsequent month or fraction thereof, capped at 100% of the tax; if no tax is due, a fixed penalty of EGP 5,000–20,000. Late payment: additional 2% monthly surcharge on the unpaid amount. Incorrect or incomplete return: fine up to EGP 50,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding tax on dividends paid by Egyptian companies to all shareholders, subject to reduced rates under an applicable double taxation agreement
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must: (1) obtain an official Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority; (2) deliver the TRC, a beneficial-ownership declaration, and a DTA relief application to the Egyptian payer before the distribution date; (3) have the Egyptian payer submit the application to the ETA and obtain confirmation, where required, before applying the reduced withholding rate; and (4) retain legally certified Arabic/English copies for at least five years. E-portal pre-registration of the TRC is strongly recommended to avoid refund litigation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 20%, treaty rates generally 10–15% for industrial royalties (trademark and recipe royalties commonly 10%). Interest on cross-border debt: statutory 20%, treaty rates usually 10–15%; arm's-length interest rate documentation is required.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 10 million aggregate related-party transactions per year for the Local File; Master File is required when the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds EGP 300 million; a simplified transfer-pricing disclosure form must be filed for cross-border related-party transactions exceeding EGP 2 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt follows a substance-over-form doctrine and applies a general anti-abuse rule (GAAR). The ETA may disregard an entity or arrangement that lacks commercial justification and is principally tax-motivated. Free-zone companies must demonstrate actual premises, qualified staff, real decision-making, and substantive operations in the free zone; failure to do so results in loss of the tax holiday and re-assessment at 22.5%. All related-party transactions, including export sales of pre-packaged hotpot soup base bricks, must be supported by contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation and benchmark analyses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating export revenue from hotpot soup base sales (e.g., issuing invoices to an offshore distributor below arm's-length prices) or overstating cost of goods sold using fictitious supplier invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of twice the evaded tax; in addition, the full tax plus a 100% late-payment surcharge is collected, and the company's tax card is suspended.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where directors sign false returns or participate in fictitious invoicing, the corporate veil is pierced; directors face civil restitution of the evaded tax, travel bans, and imprisonment under Law 91 of 2005.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominally Egyptian LLC solely to access a free-zone tax holiday or a lower DTA rate, without operational premises, employees, management, or commercial risk in Egypt, while routing hotpot base transactions through the entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA disregards the legal form, applies GAAR to re-assess 22.5% tax on deemed Egyptian-source profit, revokes the free-zone exemption, and levies an understatement penalty of up to 40% of the additional tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly liable for the re-determined tax and subjected to travel bans; criminal fraud charges are available if the misrepresentation is intentional.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Triangular trade arrangements using the Egyptian LLC to disguise the origin of funds, false invoicing, or systematic over/under-valuation of the pre-packaged hotpot brick shipments to transfer value across borders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 80 of 2002, imprisonment of up to 15 years and a fine equal to 5%–10% of the laundered amount; bank accounts are frozen and the proceeds confiscated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally face criminal liability, asset freezing, and pecuniary restitution; extradition is available under Egypt's bilateral criminal treaties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the transfer-pricing disclosure form, absence of the Local File when the annual related-party sales of hotpot soup base exceed the EGP 10 million threshold, or non-adjustment of intercompany pricing to an arm's-length margin.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA may adjust the taxable profit, disallow cross-border related-party deductions, impose an additional tax equal to 10% of the audited shortfall, and levy a fixed punitive fine of EGP 100,000 for non-filing of the disclosure form.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the return while aware of the missing transfer-pricing file can be personally liable for the tax shortfall; a court-ordered travel bar may be issued during enforcement.
